courses.title: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development

modules.title: Platform architecture, infobases and development environments

sections.title: Platform, configuration and data
sections.text:
Platform, configuration and data
Model actual 1C execution and choose an environment supporting the task being verified.
File skills and synthetic-data discipline; A1 is optional.
Draw platform, configuration and infobase boundaries.
Separate visualization, static analysis and execution.
Explain checks that OneScript cannot replace.

sections.title: The platform executes an application model
sections.text:
1C development involves more than a text language. Configuration defines metadata, forms, modules, rights and other application elements. The platform uses that definition to organize UI, storage and execution. A single BSL file is therefore not an application configuration. Access to catalog managers, documents and registers depends on metadata and execution context.
In the service desk, separate the Request type definition, request instances and operations on them. A query against a nonexistent catalog does not become valid because an editor highlights its name. An architectural error can precede a syntax error: a grammatically valid call may target an object absent from the application. Establish the model before choosing an execution location.

sections.title: Three different evidence modes
sections.text:
A visualization presents a simplified model. It can explain a causal relationship but cannot establish execution. Static analysis examines text and available descriptions without running the application scenario. Execution invokes an actual environment with a configuration, inputs and state. These modes must not silently substitute for one another.
Candidate diagrams use JavaScript and are explicitly labeled as learning models. Separately, the official platform executed ManagedApplicationModule.bsl using three in-memory synthetic records, a 105-minute sum and two negative cases. That does not prove document posting, concurrent transactions or a server cluster: the probe contains none of those mechanisms.

sections.title: Context matters more than extension
sections.text:
A .bsl extension identifies module text, not its execution location. Client form modules, server common modules and object modules expose different objects and events. P1 uses a managed application module in a separate file infobase. P8 examines client/server directives in depth; for now, record context with every example.
OneScript is a separate virtual machine with a related language. It can serve automation and a bounded subset of language exercises, but it does not automatically supply 1C metadata, managed forms or registers. A successful .os run does not prove .bsl behavior in a configuration. Compatibility requires a matrix of types, collections, conversions, exceptions and contexts before it can be offered as a substitute.

sections.title: Environment limits belong in architecture
sections.text:
Training edition has volume limits, one session and no client/server mode. It cannot establish concurrent access behavior or password authentication. The community path supports broader development tasks but requires official registration and compliance with its terms. Basic P1 requires neither a deployed server nor Nexus infrastructure changes.
Choose the smallest adequate environment: official file-mode platform for P1; separate approval for network and concurrency experiments. Preserve full version, module source, inputs and actual output. A second person can then reproduce the check and distinguish the proven mechanism from a future project.

lessons.title: File infobase and a reproducible workspace

sections.title: File infobase and a reproducible workspace
sections.text:
File infobase and a reproducible workspace
Create a disposable official workspace, verify recovery and preserve enough information to repeat the experiment.
P1.1; legitimately installed official platform.
Reproduce creation and loading of original configuration.
Verify that the destination is new.

sections.title: Reproducibility fixes the conditions
sections.text:
“Works on my machine” omits version, starting state and inputs. A repeatable experiment needs full platform version, infobase type, metadata, modules, operation order and success criteria. A course name cannot replace these details. Installed 8.3.27.2214 and downloadable Windows training 8.3.27.1508 are different builds; transferring evidence requires a separate run.
The Nexus native kit contains original empty-configuration metadata and a managed application module. It includes no proprietary application configurations or third-party records. Metadata UUIDs describe learning objects and are not licenses. Platform installers are excluded and obtained through official sources.

sections.title: Create without overwriting
sections.text:
Choose a nonexistent experiment directory before running the gate. Existing destinations are rejected rather than silently cleared. The base is created in base; recovery uses restored. No path is taken from the owner’s infobase list, and adding the experiment to the shared startup list is unnecessary.
A new directory is necessary but insufficient: the protocol must confirm it was actually used. Do not put real logins or passwords in command arguments. An empty learning infobase needs neither. If an installation requires activation or personal sign-in, leave that separate owner action explicit instead of bypassing access.

sections.title: Preserve structure and state separately
sections.text:
Exporting configuration files supports review and Git. Dumping an infobase transfers a particular infobase state. Recovery verification needs a second new instance and comparison after loading. P1 has no persisted application records, so this experiment verifies configuration and execution recovery, not future documents.
After restore, the same probe must produce the expected line again. This is stronger than simply finding a .dt file. A5/P5 will require control IDs, document counts, relations and register totals. Design evidence alongside the data model rather than after the interface.

sections.title: Read an automated protocol carefully
sections.text:
Exit code 0 says the command reported no failure; it does not establish the intended result. The gate also requires a BSL output file and exact matching contents. A syntax check needs a negative control: a deliberately broken module must be detected. Otherwise, you may be checking an empty infobase or a different module.
Preserve safe operation logs and source hashes, not licensing files or personal paths from unknown workspaces. Distinguish native AUTOMATED PASS, learner manual LIVE PASS and NOT RUN. An absence of log errors is not evidence of educational effectiveness.

sections.title: Metadata, update lifecycle and first BSL
sections.text:
Metadata, update lifecycle and first BSL
Trace a source change to actual output and check positive and negative cases.
P1.1–P1.2; ability to follow a sequence. P2 studies syntax in depth.
Distinguish working and database configurations.
Read arrays, structures and a loop in the first example.
Explain how a test rejects incorrect behavior.

sections.title: A change has multiple states
sections.text:
Editing a file does not change a running infobase. Load and check the development configuration, apply it to database configuration, then launch the application and reconcile behavior. Skipping a link leads to a common mistake: reading new source while executing the previous configuration.
The kit places the module at Ext/ManagedApplicationModule.bsl. The platform invokes ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы when a managed application starts. It registers no real documents: the array stores three structures in process memory. Exiting does not turn those values into a request table.

sections.title: Read the example through its data flow
sections.text:
A structure groups named values Код, Минуты and Статус. An array stores a sequence of structures. The For Each loop visits three elements, checks each status and adds minutes to the running sum, initially zero. After the loop, count and sum are checked: 3 and 105. Work grows in proportion to the element count.
Focus on data flow before memorizing syntax. Identify how the second request contributes 45 minutes. Removing it must change both count and total. If a modified experiment leaves output unchanged, check whether the new module was loaded and database configuration updated. Saved editor text does not establish that.

sections.title: Checks need negative cases
sections.text:
ДопустимыйСтатус accepts only New, In progress and Closed in their source Russian strings. Separate checks reject an empty string and Оплачена. Two negative inputs do not prove all future rules, but they catch overly broad behavior such as accepting every nonempty string.
ПроверитьУсловие raises an exception on a false condition, so PASS follows successful checks rather than appearing independently. The native gate also tests configuration analysis using a syntactically broken separate copy. Never change expected values merely to obtain green results: first explain the changed requirement and necessary checks.

sections.title: Output and measurable limits
sections.text:
The expected line records item count, minute total and negative-case count. Automation passes its result-file path as a startup parameter inside the new test directory. A manual launch without that parameter displays the message and leaves the application available for observation.
This demonstrates official BSL execution and one reproducible learning computation. It does not demonstrate persisted requests, transactions, Mastery or learner independence. Preserve source and actual output together; either alone leaves uncertainty about the program that ran.

sections.text:
Designer, EDT, Git and diagnostics

sections.title: A development environment is not the runtime
sections.text:
Designer ships with the platform and is the reproducible P1 path. EDT is a separate Eclipse-based environment supporting projects and Git. It can target different platform versions and infobases, but running an application still requires the platform. Having an EDT project does not establish successful application to an infobase.
At the audit date the official website offers EDT 2026.2.2. We do not claim it is installed or tested with our workspace. Redistribution rights cannot be inferred from Eclipse licensing; the product and components need a separate check. Designer is sufficient for P1; EDT remains an optional additional validation path.

sections.title: Highlighting, BSL LS and OneScript
sections.text:
BSL Language Server supplies analysis and editor capabilities. Its LGPL license and diagnostics do not turn it into a 1C engine. The candidate does not integrate it and therefore makes no BSL LS static PASS claim. Native configuration checking is a separate executed mechanism with a version and negative control.
OneScript uses MPL-2.0 and executes an independent language implementation. It may support bounded language exercises but cannot stand in for 1C forms or registers. Neither OneScript nor BSL LS is added to mandatory Nexus startup. A provider/bridge decision needs 02/01 coordination and a threat model rather than a catalog flag change.

sections.title: Git preserves an explainable change
sections.text:
A commit should connect the problem, change and verification. Preserve sources, a concise protocol and safe evidence. Exclude working infobases, licensing files, personal connection parameters and installers. Reviewers need to see the changed module and the test expectations justifying it. Project commit messages are in Russian.
Avoid diverging copies of shared definitions. The course glossary is versioned and referenced by lessons, while learning results remain course-specific. A future shared-content update must not silently reinterpret a saved attempt; it needs a new version and compatibility review.

sections.title: Diagnose from observation to hypothesis
sections.text:
When output is absent, first identify the completed stage: creation, loading, checking, update or execution. Then compare version, directory and source hash. File-access failure does not prove missing licensing; syntax failure does not prove a broken platform. State a narrow hypothesis that one safe experiment can falsify.
During author verification, access to a new infobase file was initially denied by the execution environment. The same operation on that same isolated workspace succeeded with permitted local access. We preserved the failed attempt and explanation without inventing a platform defect or touching production. Record problem → hypothesis → attempt → result → decision → regression.

lessons.title: Your first calculation: variables, assignment and output

sections.title: Your first calculation: variables, assignment and output
sections.text:
Your first calculation: variables, assignment and output
Calculate the duration of two fictional service requests in installed 1C, explain each statement and change the calculation deliberately.
Install the official training edition of 1C:Enterprise. The lab guide explains installation and creating a new empty file infobase.
Be able to open your own training infobase in Designer and distinguish it from other infobases. The applied course is not a mandatory prerequisite.
Explain how assignment evaluates its right side before updating the variable on its left.
Put a short program in the correct procedure, update the database configuration and see 75 in 1C:Enterprise.
Predict 50 after changing one input, diagnose subtraction instead of addition and independently total three durations.

sections.title: The problem: calculate a total rather than print a prepared answer
sections.text:
The service desk has two requests, planned for 30 and 45 minutes. The dispatcher needs their combined duration: 75 minutes. Сообщить(75); would display that number, but would not calculate a total. Someone would have to recalculate manually whenever a request changed. Our program stores the two inputs and then computes the sum from their current values. These are fictional training requests, with no real customer information or money.
The program uses the 1C script language, commonly designated BSL in development tools. Read and analyze the lesson in Nexus, enter the source in Designer, and observe execution in the 1C:Enterprise window. The platform calls the application startup handler and displays the message. Nexus Studio can store sources, but is unnecessary for these four statements. Colored words in a browser do not mean that 1C has executed them.
Success is more than seeing one number once. Connect the inputs 30 and 45, the addition operation and the output 75. When the second input becomes 20, the same calculation must produce 50. This change distinguishes an actual calculation from a hard-coded answer. No statement here saves a catalog item or a document: screen output and persisted infobase data are different results.

sections.title: Assignment: evaluate the right side, then update the left
sections.text:
A variable names a value the program can use. In МинутыПервойЗаявки = 30; the identifier is on the left and the numeric literal is on the right. Assignment first evaluates the right side, then puts the result into the variable on the left. After this statement, МинутыПервойЗаявки holds 30. After the second, МинутыВторойЗаявки also holds 45. Track assigned values rather than assuming values that the program has not assigned.
The third statement has an expression rather than a single literal on its right side: МинутыПервойЗаявки + МинутыВторойЗаявки. The platform reads 30 and 45, adds them, and assigns 75 to ВсегоМинут. The fourth statement passes this value to the built-in Сообщить procedure. Displaying the value does not change the total. Moving the calculation before the input assignments would break the required order of actions.
МинутыПервойЗаявки is one identifier without spaces. Its readable parts help a person, but do not determine the type of the value. An unquoted 30 is a number; a quoted "30" is text. Both inputs in this lab must be numbers. A semicolon ends each statement. The argument to Сообщить goes inside parentheses. Copy identifiers as a whole: visually similar Cyrillic and Latin letters can form different names.

sections.title: Where the program belongs and why saving text is not enough
sections.text:
The managed application module contains code associated with the application as a whole. ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы is an event handler called by the platform when the application starts. Place the four statements between Процедура ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы() and КонецПроцедуры. These boundary lines are not part of the four-statement calculation, but provide its startup context.
A new empty infobase may not yet have this handler. The lab therefore provides the complete six-line module. If an infobase already contains your own handlers, preserve them and create a separate empty infobase for this first experiment instead of replacing its existing module. You do not need to save the four statements in Studio, export an archive and reload the source after every edit.
Saving in Designer preserves the editable configuration. The running application uses the database configuration, which must receive your changes before a new session starts. Close any open 1C:Enterprise user window, save in Designer, press F7 to update the database configuration, confirm the update if prompted, then press F5 to start. The training edition permits one simultaneous session; do not open multiple user sessions for this infobase.

sections.title: Test the idea by changing one input
sections.text:
Write your prediction before running: 30 + 45 = 75. Compare it with the platform message. Replacing 45 with 20 in the second statement changes only the second request duration. The third statement still adds the two variables, so the next saved, updated and restarted version should display 50. Restore 45 before the following experiment, keeping the inputs for each observation clear.
Consider the faulty expression ВсегоМинут = МинутыПервойЗаявки - МинутыВторойЗаявки; It is syntactically valid but solves a different problem. With 30 and 45 it produces −15. A syntax check need not reject a calculation that misunderstands the requirement. Comparing actual output with the expected 75 detects this error. Correct the operator, preserve the expected result, and rerun with the same inputs.
Extend addition by assigning a third duration, 15, to another variable and including it in the sum. The prediction for 30, 45 and 15 is 90. First repeat the worked example, then change one known input, and finally solve the independent task with 10, 25 and 5. This progression tests whether you can transfer the method to new values rather than merely copy a familiar statement.

sections.title: Independent task
sections.text:
Three requests take 10, 25 and 5 minutes. Calculate their total using meaningful variable names. Then check the case where the second takes 0 minutes. Predict both results before running.
Obtain 40 and 15. Separate input assignments, calculation and output. Preserve the source and actual platform messages without claiming that Nexus automatically verified the external run.
A zero duration must not remove the other requests from the sum.

Designer and Nexus
Both results were observed, or a specific mismatch recorded.
Save the module in your infobase. To back it up, close the user session and choose Designer → Administration → Dump infobase…, using a new .dt filename. Return to Nexus for the self-check and attest only after performing your own run.

sections.title: From inputs to observed output
sections.text:
Assign inputs
Two assignments establish durations 30 and 45. The total has not yet been calculated.
Evaluate the right side
The expression reads both current values and evaluates 30 + 45 = 75.
Assign the total
ВсегоМинут receives 75. The input variables remain 30 and 45.
Display a message
Сообщить reads ВсегоМинут and displays 75. No infobase object is written.

sections.title: Mistakes and diagnosis
sections.text:
I opened Studio and am waiting for 75.
Use installed 1C Designer and then run the application. Studio stores text; the browser does not execute BSL.
I pasted the statements after КонецПроцедуры.
Move the four statements inside ПриНачалеРаботыСистемы, preserving one matching procedure boundary pair.
I changed 45 to 20 but still see 75.
Close the old application window, update the database configuration with F7 and start again. Check the selected infobase name.
The syntax check succeeded but output is −15.
Inspect the operator: subtraction is valid syntax but does not satisfy the addition requirement. Do not change the expected 75 to fit faulty code.

sections.title: Review and next step
sections.text:

Show where the source is edited, where execution happens and where the result appears.
Next: value types, including the distinction between the number 30 and the text "30".

lessons.title: Types, Undefined, Null and explicit conversion

sections.title: Types, Undefined, Null and explicit conversion
sections.text:
Types, Undefined, Null and explicit conversion
Separate absent values from a valid zero and check input before evaluating it, without relying on variable names or accidental conversion.
P2.1; functions, expressions and the real native gate.
Inspect value types with TypeOf/ТипЗнч.
Distinguish Undefined, Null, strings, numbers and domain validity.
Check explicit conversion and a failing conversion case.

sections.title: Value type and field requirements
sections.text:
BSL’s flexible typing allows a variable to hold different value types over time. A program must still decide what a particular operation permits. For minutes we first check ТипЗнч(Значение)=Тип("Число"), then the range 0..1440. String "30" resembles a number but fails this contract. Parsing it requires separate rules rather than silently passing it to arithmetic.
Separate three questions: the value’s type, whether an operation accepts that type, and whether the value satisfies a domain rule. -1 is a Number but is not an admissible duration here. Zero is also a Number and is permitted. Variable names, highlighting and presentation answer none of these questions. Record type and expected decision separately from displayed text.

sections.title: Different forms of absence
sections.text:
Undefined and Null have different types, verified by separate native cases. Undefined can represent an unavailable value; Null also matters in data handling, including future query results. This lesson does not declare them interchangeable, equal to zero or equivalent to JavaScript null. It compares their types; query-specific Null semantics are studied in P7.
An empty catalog reference is another distinct situation. It retains that catalog’s reference type but identifies no particular customer. A2 disallows it in a request. Empty strings, numeric zero, False and empty references must not be grouped under one vague “empty” rule when field requirements differ. Establish field meaning before choosing a validation function.

sections.title: ValueIsFilled is not universal validation
sections.text:
On the tested platform, ЗначениеЗаполнено(0) returns False. Using it as the sole duration validator would reject an allowed zero. ЭтоЧислоМинут instead checks type and range separately. This illustrates meaning-driven validation, not a blanket rejection of ValueIsFilled: it is appropriate for the mandatory customer reference in this workspace.
A useful input matrix includes zero, an ordinary number, the upper boundary, negative and excessive values, a string and Undefined. Record a distinct expectation for each. A few positive cases cannot reveal zero being mistaken for absence or text passing unnoticed. Test counts are useful only alongside their actual meaning and exercised boundaries.

sections.title: Conversion is an explicit decision that can fail
sections.text:
Число("12") returns 12 in the native case. Число("не число") raises an exception; a separate Try/Except block confirms that rejection. Do not continue with a variable’s accidental previous value or declare the input valid after a conversion failure. Parsing failure differs from a domain rejection: even a successfully parsed -1 must still fail the minutes rule.
Parsing localized fractional text needs a separate input-format contract. No claim is made that every comma, space or currency symbol is accepted identically. P2.5 separates formatting from values; this basic validator expects an already numeric input. Preserve synthetic input, decision and observed exception rather than real user data. This keeps the experiment repeatable and safe.

sections.text:
ЭтоЧислоМинут(0); ЭтоЧислоМинут("30"); ЭтоЧислоМинут(Неопределено)
True; False; False.
The contract separates parsing from domain validation.

sections.text:

There is no contradiction: the functions answer different questions.
A mandatory reference and a numeric duration need different rules.

lessons.title: Conditions, Boolean expressions and decision tables

sections.title: Conditions, Boolean expressions and decision tables
sections.text:
Conditions, Boolean expressions and decision tables
Build a complete decision table for request duration and verify branch order, types and boundaries in real BSL.
P2.1–P2.2; type versus validity and the ЭтоЧислоМинут function.
Translate requirements into nonoverlapping input classes.
Explain If/ElsIf/Else and And/Or/Not.
Find a boundary defect through a counterexample rather than random trials.

sections.title: Define the rule before coding
sections.text:
КлассДлительности has an explicit contract. Nonnumeric inputs and numbers outside 0..1440 are rejected. Zero maps to NoCost; positive values through 60 inclusive is Short; values above 60 through 1440 is Long. This is a learning classification, not a medical, employment or financial standard. Changing class names or boundaries requires changing requirements and tests deliberately.
Before reading the implementation, build a table for -1, 0, 1, 60, 61, 1440, 1441 and string "60", recording types separately. The table reveals missing classes or ambiguous boundaries. An ordinary input such as 30 cannot distinguish the intended algorithm from one that treats 60 as Long or accepts textual input unexpectedly.

sections.title: Branch ordering changes behavior
sections.text:
The first branch calls ЭтоЧислоМинут and rejects an invalid input. Zero is handled next, then <=60, then the remaining admissible range. An If/ElsIf chain takes the first matching branch. Reaching the final Else establishes that type and range are valid, the value is nonzero and it exceeds 60. These accumulated facts explain the final branch.
Placing a broad <=60 branch before the zero case classifies zero as Short. Replacing <= with < makes 60 Long. Both variants can pass syntax checking. Include inputs that distinguish these implementations. For each experiment, record the first incorrect result and its cause instead of adding arbitrary exceptions that conceal an ordering defect.

sections.title: Boolean expressions and safe preconditions
sections.text:
Value>=0 And Value<=1440 requires both bounds simultaneously. Or can combine reasons for rejection, while Not reverses a Boolean predicate. Read a compound expression as a claim about a particular input. When combining business rules, decide whether both or at least one must hold before choosing an operator. Parentheses make grouping explicit.
This implementation returns early on a wrong type before comparing numeric bounds. Correctness does not depend on side effects or guesses about right-hand evaluation. These exercises use True/False; query-specific Null behavior is not imported automatically. If an input can represent a third special meaning, handle it before applying a two-valued decision table.

sections.title: What the evidence establishes
sections.text:
The native suite checks -1, 0, 60, 61, 1440, 1441 and string "60" in seven separate P2.3 cases. They exercise important current boundaries, not every number, fractional duration or future textual format. The goal is to justify test selection and explain limitations. A PASS count without its actual input set provides less information.
Proposed properties could include every admissible positive input <=60 being Short, rejected input leaving infobase state unchanged, and repeated calls returning the same class. These remain proposed until tested. This pure function classifies a value and writes no document. A2’s BeforeWrite rules are a separate boundary and cannot be declared verified by classification alone.

lessons.title: Loops: tracing, termination and boundary datasets

sections.title: Loops: tracing, termination and boundary datasets
sections.text:
Loops: tracing, termination and boundary datasets
Calculate an aggregate, explain loop termination and check empty or invalid input without modifying source values.
P2.1–P2.3; valid-minute predicates and branching.
Match For, While and For Each to tasks.
Trace accumulators and counters.
Explain Break/Continue and verify that the input array remains unchanged.

sections.title: Repetition needs state and a stopping argument
sections.text:
A loop repeats actions, but a useful algorithm explains what changes and when repetition stops. For suits a known range; For Each traverses collection elements; While checks a condition before each step. The construct alone proves nothing. Explain progress toward termination for While and the finite source collection for traversal.
СуммаМинут accepts an array of numeric durations. Its initial total is zero and each valid element is added once. For [30,45,0], accumulator states are 0→30→75→75. The array still contains three elements: the function neither removes nor overwrites them. It processes an in-memory array, not automatically every document in the infobase. A2’s separate code checks real persisted documents.

sections.title: An invariant locates the first wrong step
sections.text:
After processing the first k elements, the accumulator equals their sum. This invariant also explains an empty array: no step executes and the result remains zero. An arbitrary initial total or skipping the first item can produce a wrong final result without revealing the cause. A k→item→before/after trace locates the first divergence.
Each element passes ЭтоЧислоМинут before addition. A negative element raises an exception instead of being ignored silently. That is the selected contract: a partial dataset must not resemble a complete valid aggregate. Collecting errors while continuing is another possible design, but it needs a separate result structure and tests. Do not mix strategies without changing the task explicitly.

sections.title: Boundaries and loop control
sections.text:
The verified For loop from 1 through 3 visits 1,2,3 and sums to 6. A While counter starting at zero and incrementing while <3 finishes at 3. Termination follows from the counter update, not from hoping someone stops the program. Bound manual experiments in advance; hanging a process is not a useful infinite-loop test.
Continue skips the remainder of the current iteration; Break ends the loop. A native 1..5 example skips 2 and stops before adding 4, so only 1 and 3 contribute and the result is 4. Five is never considered after Break. This trace distinguishes the commands more precisely than saying both “exit the loop.”

sections.title: Evidence coverage and remaining work
sections.text:
Seven P2.4 cases check aggregation, preserved input count, an empty array, inclusive For bounds, While termination, Continue/Break and rejection of an invalid item. This finite set is not a large-data performance measurement. A simple sum visits elements proportionally to collection size; field p95, server execution and concurrent collection changes are not measured.
For your own practice, use a separate copy and predict results before running. A printed PASS does not prove the body executed: the initial condition may have been false. Use ordinary, empty and invalid inputs and inspect intermediate state. Preserve a failed trace, then explain the change that fixes its first incorrect iteration without destroying the earlier experiment.

lessons.title: Numbers, dates, strings and explicit interchange formats

sections.title: Numbers, dates, strings and explicit interchange formats
sections.text:
Numbers, dates, strings and explicit interchange formats
Separate values from presentation, verify numeric/date calculations and define boundaries for localized input.
P2.1–P2.4; numeric input contracts and repeatable cases.
Check decimal computation without importing JavaScript assumptions.
Produce an explicit textual number representation.
Construct dates from components and explain seconds, calendar meaning and timezone limits.

sections.title: A numeric value differs from its string
sections.text:
On the tested BSL platform, 0.1+0.2 equals 0.3. This comes from an actual native case, not a browser calculation. Do not import another runtime’s binary or formatting assumptions without testing them. The learning formula Minutes*Rate/60 yields 300 for 30 minutes at an hourly rate of 600. Establish units, evaluation order and input preconditions first.
УчебнаяСтоимость assumes numeric inputs and is not a general financial calculator. It defines no currency, tax, negative-rate validation or rounding policy. Correct output 300 for one case proves none of those rules. The P2 duration predicate checks type and range, not integrality; fractional-minute policy must likewise be an explicit requirement rather than an implication of the field name.

sections.title: Separate formatting from parsing
sections.text:
Формат(12.5, "ЧДЦ=2; ЧРД=.; ЧГ=0") produces string "12.50" in the native case: two fractional digits, a decimal point and no grouping are explicit. The original value remains numeric; formatting returns a presentation. If another system consumes the text, define an interchange format and check that consumer. Attractive interface output is not automatically an agreed protocol.
Strings "12,50", "12.50" and "12 500" can depend on input rules and locale. This lesson does not promise identical conversion for arbitrary text. An explicit output format does not automatically make parsing reversible. Specify a parser, allowed separators, error behavior and range. Replacing every comma with a period is not proven support for all locales; enumerate accepted and rejected inputs first.

sections.title: Construct dates from components and define their meaning
sections.text:
The native suite constructs Дата(2026,10,31,9,30,0). It checks year, month and day separately, then adds 60 seconds and verifies a difference of 60. Components avoid ambiguous strings such as 03/04/2026, which can mean March or April depending on convention. The exercise uses a fixed date rather than the computer’s changing clock.
A calendar value alone establishes no UTC or external-timezone agreement. For interchange, define whether it represents local event time, a date-only document attribute or an instant on a shared timeline. Timezone and daylight-saving transitions were not tested in this workspace. Adding 60 seconds successfully at one calendar value does not complete an integration design.

sections.title: Strings, units and closing the P2 package
sections.text:
СтрДлина("Заявка") returns 6 in a separate native case. That is not a UTF-8 byte count or a universal guarantee about visible characters in every Unicode sequence. Text length, SHA256 and encoded file size answer different questions. Customer codes C001 and document numbers A200001 are identifiers, not quantities to add arithmetically.
Close P2 by combining expression, type, branch, loop and representation tables. Its 35 cases form part of a 46-case suite that also exercises A2 relationships and persistence. The gate checks correct code, a syntax defect and a separate semantic mutation. It establishes the listed mechanisms on build 8.3.27.2214, not every platform version, learner authorship or server execution. Preserve your copy, source hash, expectations and output together.

sections.title: Module contexts and exports
sections.text:
Module contexts and exports
Extract a common-module computation contract and check call availability by context.
onec.p2; P2: types, branching, loops and numeric boundaries.
Extract a common-module computation contract and check call availability by context.
Map module→data→call for a request calculation.
Extract the form calculation with explicit minutes and rate.

sections.title: A module belongs to a context
sections.text:
BSL text belongs to an application, object, form or common module. Placement determines available data: an object module sees the attributes of its object, while a common module does not receive them automatically. Pass minutes and rate explicitly so calculation does not depend on an open form. Identical function names in different modules do not make the functions identical.
The service-desk calculation may be called from a card, document and report. Separate formulas let one fix leave two old implementations behind. A common computation contract avoids that divergence but needs explicit inputs. List every caller and verify equal units, parameter meaning and result type rather than merely matching function names.

sections.title: Export defines a call surface
sections.text:
Export permits calls from an available external context; it does not create an unrestricted network API. A common module has separate client, server and server-call settings. A pure calculation needs only the necessary contexts. A public function validates its inputs even when a screen has already performed similar checks.
Describe a function by inputs, preconditions, result and permitted changes. Cost uses numeric minutes/rate, admissible ranges, a rounded number and unchanged input collections. This description selects tests before implementation. If failure returns another type, callers must know explicitly or an error can accidentally participate in arithmetic. A stable contract makes substitution and review possible.

sections.title: Make dependencies visible
sections.text:
Hidden reads of a current document or global variable make a calculation state-dependent. Tests with identical inputs may then depend on a previous window or execution order. Extract the data transformation first and the object-reading adapter second. If a function accesses the infobase, expose that fact in its contract and test it against a separate record set.
Checking mutation needs more than comparing variable names: two variables can refer to one collection. Snapshot important fields and nested elements before execution, then compare the source afterwards. Run another function on the same input to expose hidden contamination. Keep each test’s setup independent so changing test order cannot alter the outcome.

sections.title: Check an availability matrix
sections.text:
Record caller module, directive, expected outcome and required common-module setting in a matrix. A compile error for an unavailable call is more useful than enabling every flag. Test an allowed call too: denying everything is not a correct implementation. A client context in a file infobase does not prove traversal of a network server.
A semantic negative control differs from a syntax error. Replacing addition with subtraction may compile but must change a named assertion’s result. Keep compilation and executed assertions as separate outcomes. Unavailable platforms, timeouts and incomplete case lists cannot confirm missing results. Preserve original and mutated source hashes and identify the particular assertion that detects the defect.

sections.title: Procedures, functions and parameters
sections.text:
Procedures, functions and parameters
Design a calculation function with explicit inputs, return value and mutation contract.
onec.p2; P2: types, branching, loops and numeric boundaries.
Design a calculation function with explicit inputs, return value and mutation contract.
Specify result and parameter types.
Compare normal and Val parameters with a number and an array.

sections.title: Procedures act, functions return
sections.text:
A procedure suits a command; a function suits a computed value. Return ends the current function call, not the whole session. Do not mix a successful result with an error-message string: callers need a stable result type. For request cost, agree on a number for success and an exception for invalid ranges.
The service-desk calculation may be called from a card, document and report. Separate formulas let one fix leave two old implementations behind. A common computation contract avoids that divergence but needs explicit inputs. List every caller and verify equal units, parameter meaning and result type rather than merely matching function names.

sections.title: Parameters and mutation
sections.text:
A normal parameter permits changing the passed variable; Val restricts reassignment of the parameter variable itself. Val does not turn a mutable collection into a deep copy: adding an element may remain visible outside. If input must be preserved, construct a new collection or avoid mutating methods. Compare contents before and after, not merely the variable reference.

Explain the first with the field name; preserve the second for a developer. Do not return zero from a catch-all handler: zero resembles a successful cost and corrupts later totals.

sections.title: Entity and key
sections.text:
A customer outlives one request. Its internal reference distinguishes it from another item even with the same name. An external code supports imports but needs its own uniqueness scope. Define which event creates a customer and which only updates the existing presentation.
Model changes as well as creation. Customers can be renamed, services repriced, and requests can retain earlier agreed terms. List these events separately to identify catalog data, document snapshots and historical facts. This prevents silently updating every linked request when only current presentation or a current service offering should change.

sections.title: Normalization is not a business decision
sections.text:
Trimming spaces and case normalization can help compare codes but may collapse distinct identifiers. Normalized names do not prove identity. Define a unique teaching codeC001 and reject collisions with a different entity. Repeating an import must not increase item count.
Internal identity and external code solve different problems. References connect infobase objects; codes support imported correspondence. Define uniqueness scope, case handling and absence policy. Two systems can reuse one code for different customers, requiring sender scope or a mapping table. A name search alone cannot resolve this ambiguity safely or justify replacing an existing entity.

sections.title: References preserve relationships
sections.text:
A document stores a customer reference. Renaming should change presentation without breaking requests. Replacing the reference with a string loses relational identity and complicates updates. Key migration needs a mapping and checks of dependent objects; mass renaming alone is insufficient.
Keep empty references, missing items and deletion-marked objects distinct and define each outcome. An old request must not silently point to a newly created lookalike after reseeding. Compare identities and document relationships before/after; use labels only for human readability. A valid-looking card can otherwise conceal broken history or a duplicate entity.

Seed twice and compare references, count and attributes. Add equal names with different codes to expose name-based lookup errors. Concurrent creation under one code needs a transactional solution; single-user repetition does not prove it. P10 addresses that boundary.
Use an ordinary customer, an equal-named second customer and a request-free third customer. Test lookup, rename, reseed and selection. This set exposes implementations that only work when labels happen to be unique. Reopen the source separately afterwards: independent copies are proven by preserved records, not different labels in a launcher list.

sections.title: Facts by key
sections.text:
An information register suits rates by service and time. Service is a dimension, rate a resource, and period adds history. An attribute stores extra description rather than replacing the key. Start from “which rate applied toS1 atD”; one current card price cannot answer the historical question.
Choose a register from the data question. “Which rate applied?” needs keyed temporal state;“how much was delivered this week?” needs turnover;“what obligation remains?” needs balance. sections.title: Periodicity limits distinguishable states
sections.text:
Two records for one service in one period follow the key policy. Daily periodicity cannot distinguish two intraday changes under the same key. Do not substitute current time just to bypass a collision. Choose required precision and test exactly at a rate-change boundary.
Dimensions define slices, resources measured quantities, and recorders provenance where supported. Adding a dimension changes keys and granularity: customer totals may split by service. Define old-data treatment and grand-total reconciliation before restructuring. New granularity is more than another displayed column; it changes writes, uniqueness and the interpretation of historical records.

sections.title: A repeatable transformation
sections.text:
Posting transforms the current document into a movement set. Identical input should yield an equivalent set regardless of repetition. Compare dimensions, resources, periods and recorder—not merely one total. Opposite duplicates can cancel numerically while leaving invalid records.
Choose a register from the data question. “Which rate applied?” needs keyed temporal state;“how much was delivered this week?” needs turnover;“what obligation remains?” needs balance. Dimensions define slices, resources measured quantities, and recorders provenance where supported. Adding a dimension changes keys and granularity: customer totals may split by service. sections.title: Failures must not mix versions

Failure between removing old and writing new records must not leave a partial effect. Inject failure only in a new copy and test atomicity. Reread document/register in a fresh session. Transactions and locks address different concerns: one change’s consistency versus interacting concurrent changes.
Time boundaries belong in specifications. State uses an as-of moment, turnover an interval, and movements an agreed period. Test before the first fact, exactly at a change and after it. Equal totals without matching identities do not prove correctness: errors for different customers can cancel numerically while allocations remain wrong.

sections.title: A query expresses a set
sections.text:
1C query language addresses the metadata model, not arbitrarySQLfor modifying internal tables. SELECT chooses fields, FROM defines the source, andWHERE defines conditions. Begin with expected identities and values rather than selecting everything and hoping to understand later.
Every query starts with a set specification: row granularity, required fields, scope, identities and multiplicity. Reconcile a small source set manually. Syntax correctness cannot detect lost customers or multiplied sums. Inspect identities and types before totals, which may match accidentally when two defects compensate. Keep this independent oracle beside every query revision.

sections.title: Pass values as parameters
sections.text:
Do not concatenate customer names or dates into query text. SetParameter supplies a typed value separately from structure. A customer reference is not its display string. A parameter cannot stand in for an arbitrary field name: choose structure from an allowlist and keep user values parameterized.
Parameters separate structure/values without defining business meaning automatically. References, names and external codes differ. Dates carry time and agreed boundaries. Choose dynamic fields from a structural allowlist, not user text. Specify each parameter’s type, empty-value policy and an example yielding zero rows without changing data. This tests the contract rather than parser acceptance alone.

sections.title: Periods have precise boundaries
sections.text:
UseDate>=Start ANDDate<End for an agreed half-open interval. IncludeStart and excludeEnd. A daily query must account for document time. Ordinary rows do not expose a last-second error; add records exactly on both boundaries.
Joins and aggregation affect multiplicity differently. Joining two detail sets can multiply rows; grouping can hide the cause behind one wrong sum. Inspect intermediate membership before resources. Respect virtual-table semantics/parameters and temporary-table context/lifetime. Neither mechanism is a universal optimization trick. Explain which problem it solves and verify equivalent values before measuring speed.

sections.title: Result and cursor differ
sections.text:
Execute returns a query result; Select creates traversal; Unload materializes a value table. Choose by volume and needed operations. An empty result is not inherently an error. Reconcile identities, types, count and sum, then verify reading did not modify documents.
Compare performance only after equivalence. Freeze data, versions, call count, cache conditions and repeated timing. A small local experiment does not establish field p95. Reject speedups caused by dropped rows or permission checks. Preserve rejected variants, reasons and the correct baseline so later optimization does not repeat a known defect. Report observed metrics without broadening their scope.

A left join preserves all customers. Missing right-side fields areNULL, not an empty reference orUndefined. AWHEREcondition on the right table can discard these rows and defeat the intended behavior. Place conditions according to meaning rather than brevity.
Parameters separate structure/values without defining business meaning automatically. References, names and external codes differ. Dates carry time and agreed boundaries. Choose dynamic fields from a structural allowlist, not user text. Specify each parameter’s type, empty-value policy and an example yielding zero rows without changing data. This tests the contract rather than parser acceptance alone.

sections.title: Grouping selects granularity
sections.text:
GROUPBYCustomer collapses documents into customer totals. Name and reference differ: grouping by name can merge distinct customers. DISTINCTis not a universal cure for a bad join; it can hide the defect and discard legitimate equal rows. Fix relationships and aggregation granularity.
Joins and aggregation affect multiplicity differently. Joining two detail sets can multiply rows; grouping can hide the cause behind one wrong sum. Inspect intermediate membership before resources. Respect virtual-table semantics/parameters and temporary-table context/lifetime. Neither mechanism is a universal optimization trick. Explain which problem it solves and verify equivalent values before measuring speed.

sections.title: Intermediate sets need contracts

A temporary table stores intermediate results within an execution context and can support reuse. It is not a persistent catalog. Specify fields, keys and expected multiplicity. Materializing all columns or all source rows can hurt performance; select only required data with justified filtering.

sections.title: Forms hold a representation
sections.text:
A managed form has attributes and controls; an application object has logic and persisted state. Form values can be intermediate and unsaved. Equal field names do not create one variable in every context. Trace where minutes came from and when they become a persisted document value.
A managed form is an interaction boundary, not the only data source. Values occupy form buffers, objects and persisted records at different times. Trace read, edit, transfer and write to identify unsaved snapshots. Refresh must not silently replace user input with another request’s state. Distinguish visible values from accepted business state throughout the workflow.

sections.title: Conversion is explicit
sections.text:
On the server, FormAttributeToValuecan obtain an application object from a suitable form attribute. Returning data also requires proper conversion. Do not assume form data exposes every object method. Identify actual type and allowed context rather than moving everything to the client to silence an error.
Context determines available operations and required inputs. Pure calculations need numbers; document reads need identity and an available server environment; focus handling needsUI. Do not pass whole forms instead of designing minimal contracts. Specify serialized inputs, outputs and reliable-side validation independently of client hints. Context availability and permission authorization remain separate concerns.

sections.title: UIvalidation does not protect writes
sections.text:
The form may highlight bad ranges before submission, but the object boundary must enforce mandatory rules. Client data can become stale between read and write. Important operations need an agreed server-side version/state check. A new screen must not bypassP5preservation rules.
Bind asynchronous actions to a specific intent/version. Users can close forms, edit data or start another operation while awaiting replies. Late responses must validate relevance before acting. UIcancellation does not promise rollback of committed server work. Separate pending, accepted, unknown, rejected and canceled states with distinct verification scenarios rather than one ambiguous success flag.

sections.title: Test two routes
sections.text:
Create a valid request through the form and programmatically; outcomes should agree. Submit invalid data by both routes. Reopen and compare fields. If presentation is stale, refresh it through the agreed event rather than rewriting the database merely to synchronize the screen.
Test both expected and unexpected event ordering: delays, double-clicks, cancel and closing with unsaved input. Reconcile effect count and database state through fresh reads. File-mode compilation of client directives proves only that context; it does not measure network routing, physical mobile acceptance or isolatedStudioBSLexecution. Record these boundaries so successful checks are not overstated.

Asynchrony and cancellation
Handle asynchronous confirmation, cancellation and stale replies without duplicate writes.
onec.p7; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
Handle asynchronous confirmation, cancellation and stale replies without duplicate writes.
AnswerYes and execute one operation.

sections.title: Continuations run later
sections.text:
An asynchronous dialog returns control before the user answers. Decision-dependent logic belongs in its continuation rather than the next line as if synchronous. Meanwhile, the form may close, data may change or another request may start. Include those states in the operation contract.
A managed form is an interaction boundary, not the only data source. Values occupy form buffers, objects and persisted records at different times. Trace read, edit, transfer and write to identify unsaved snapshots. Refresh must not silently replace user input with another request’s state. Distinguish visible values from accepted business state throughout the workflow.

sections.title: Bind confirmation to intent
sections.text:
Preserve request identity and the confirmed snapshot. Before acting, check form and intent validity. An oldYesmust not authorize a new request; double-clicking must not create a duplicate. Use explicitpending/accepted/cancelledstate instead of one flag that conflates attempts.
Context determines available operations and required inputs. Pure calculations need numbers; document reads need identity and an available server environment; focus handling needsUI. Do not pass whole forms instead of designing minimal contracts. Specify serialized inputs, outputs and reliable-side validation independently of client hints. Context availability and permission authorization remain separate concerns.

sections.title: Cancellation has observable effects
sections.text:
No, dialog close and form cancellation must not initiate a write. Once a server operation has committed, localUIcancel need not reverse it: show actual state and a verification route. A closed window does not prove server-effect cancellation. Distinguish timeout and environment unavailability.
Bind asynchronous actions to a specific intent/version. Users can close forms, edit data or start another operation while awaiting replies. Late responses must validate relevance before acting. UIcancellation does not promise rollback of committed server work. Separate pending, accepted, unknown, rejected and canceled states with distinct verification scenarios rather than one ambiguous success flag.

sections.title: Tests control event ordering
sections.text:
TestYes, No, double-click, response after close and two replies arriving in reverse order. Tie each to its ownIDand state. One fast success does not test asynchrony: use a controlled delay in a safe stand and verify no late write. An explanatory event diagram is notBSLexecution.
Test both expected and unexpected event ordering: delays, double-clicks, cancel and closing with unsaved input. Reconcile effect count and database state through fresh reads. File-mode compilation of client directives proves only that context; it does not measure network routing, physical mobile acceptance or isolatedStudioBSLexecution. Record these boundaries so successful checks are not overstated.

sections.title: A schema describes data
sections.text:
DCS separates data description, settings, layout and output. A schema defines datasets, fields, relationships and parameters. TheMinutes resource specifies aggregation rather than merely a numeric column. Define dataset granularity and a three-document expectation before using a designer.
Define the question and granularity before composition. Customer-minute sums, average document cost and open-request counts need distinct resources/denominators. Similar-looking reports are not interchangeable. Use uneven groups and independent calculations to expose averaging/grouping errors that symmetric toy examples can hide. Check underlying identities before interpreting the final visual representation.

sections.title: Resources depend on granularity
sections.text:
An already customer-grouped dataset can be summed again only with correct multiplicity. A bad join doubles resources beforeDCS. Check raw query rows before report groupings. A computed field with a nice name cannot repair lost or extra records.
Schema describes available data, settings select retrieval/presentation, and output produces a result. Changing one level does not silently authorize changing another. Record parameters, variant, time and units. Saved settings usually are not frozen data snapshots; new documents can legitimately change the same variant. Preserve membership and observed values for reproducibility as well as the configuration of the report.

sections.title: Settings differ from the source set
sections.text:
One schema can support multiple report variants. Users change available fields, filters and groupings without silently gaining forbidden data scope. Check permissions and dataset restrictions separately. Preserve variant and parameters so another reviewer reproduces the same question.
External components and exports cross distinct boundaries. Processors execute code and need provenance, authority and environment checks. Printed files present data under edition constraints. An external processor is a program component, not a safe table simply because a menu opens it. Specify inputs, modified objects, files, network and output. Use original teaching source. Unknown emailed code must not run on the main computer merely for inspection.

sections.title: Locks and concurrent changes
sections.text:
Locks and concurrent changes
Protect a balance check against concurrent changes and reproduce two-transaction ordering.
onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
Protect a balance check against concurrent changes and reproduce two-transaction ordering.
Reproduce the unsafe schedule in a model.
Protect read and write in a permitted stand.

sections.title: Individually correct, collectively wrong
sections.text:
Two operations each read balance 10 and spend 7. Each passes alone; combined balance−4breaks the rule. A post-read check without coordinated locking does not prevent the second transaction. Starting a transaction alone does not specify lock scope. Draw read A→readB→write A→writeBbefore choosing anAPI.
Engineering quality follows invariants, not absence of exceptions. Balance uses admissible amounts, permissions authorized scope, diagnostics explainable failure without leaks. Specify what survives errors and concurrent actions. Positive cases prove utility; negative cases prove boundaries. Denying everything is not a universally correct security implementation. Evidence needs both operational success and correctly bounded rejection.

sections.title: Locks apply to data
sections.text:
Managed locking identifies a data space and dimension values. Lock invariant-related data before deciding. Too-wide locks reduce concurrency; too-narrow locks miss conflicts. Scope depends on register, mode and operation; there is no universal line suitable for every solution.
Transactions, locks and authorization solve different problems. Atomicity coordinates one operation, locking interacting operations, and rights constrain subjects. None proves the others. Identify decision point, read data and authorized actor for each failure scenario. Choose minimal protection rather than enabling every capability or broadening privileges. A context compile check is not a multi-user access proof.

sections.title: Consistent ordering reduces deadlocks
sections.text:
Two operations locking A/Bin opposite order can deadlock. Agree on stable-key order and keep transactions short. A timeout is failure, not a successful spend. Retrying needs idempotency and a fresh state read; blindly repeating external effects can duplicate them.
Measurement/observability must preserve privacy. Use synthetic IDs, bounded logs and defined metrics. Passwords/tokens are unnecessary even for leak demonstrations; use canaries. One timing is not p95, and one profile result does not cover every role/configuration combination. Keep raw diagnostics restricted and publish only sufficient sanitized evidence tied to the actual test environment.

sections.title: Two sessions need separate evidence
sections.text:
Single-sessiontrainingcannot prove this scenario. In a permitted multi-session stand, control barriers and record both traces and final balance. From 10, one spend 7 succeeds; the second rereads and rejects, result 3. Test an independent customer to show the lock does not block everything.
Security acceptance needs discriminating tests in a permitted environment. Races need two controlled sessions, roles allowed work plus bypass attempts, and isolation denial of a specific resource. Preserve traces/post-failure state and repeat a successful control. Unsupported environments yieldNOTRUN; static analysis or diagrams cannot automatically fill that evidence gap. Report the remaining gate explicitly.

sections.title: Exchange is an external boundary
sections.text:
AnHTTPrequest crosses into another participant’s failures and lifecycle. Specify method, path, body schema, response codes and size limits. A connection is not an accepted request; a 200 with a malformed body also fails the application contract. Do not send real data to public teaching services.
Integration crosses independently failing participants. Replies can be lost after acceptance, servers can reject business rules, and schedules can repeat work. Contracts need intent identity, state, limits and unknown-outcome resolution as well as body format. Specify those cases before choosingHTTP, serialization or job APIs. A successful transport call alone cannot establish the business outcome.

sections.title: Policy selects addresses
sections.text:
A user-suppliedURLmust not grant server code arbitrary internal-network/file access. Use a fixed loopback mock without secrets; it is not a production endpoint. RealHTTPSrequires certificate validation and redirect policy. DisablingTLSvalidation to make tests green is unacceptable.
Serialized input remains untrusted data. After parsing, validate schema version, required fields, types, ranges and size. Resolve external customer keys through an agreed mapping, not similar names. Never execute input or permit arbitrary addresses. A fixed local mock and synthetic payload suffice for the lab without real secrets or public external services.

sections.title: Responses can be ambiguous
sections.text:
A timeout after sending does not reveal whether the remote side accepted the request. Blind retry can duplicate work. Use a requestIDand verification/retry policy. Distinguish transport failure, business 4 xx, temporary 5 xxand schema failure. Log safe IDs rather than tokens or complete payloads.
Repeatability binds acceptance registry and result. Equal key/content returns the prior document; different content conflicts. CommitDoneand document consistently to avoid false success or duplication after failures. External effects need their own protocol. Batch continuation points likewise commit with results rather than prematurely skipping work. Test failure between these steps, not only clean completion.

Prepare valid 200, 400, 500, delay and oversized-body cases. Set expectations before running theBSLclient. The mock inspects method/path but does not replace the 1C platform. Browserfetchor aJSmodel is not execution ofHTTPConnection.
Control replies and ordering: success, schema rejection, temporary error, timeout, retry and cancel. Mocks prove the simulated peer contract; actualBSLclients prove platformAPIexecution. Manual procedure calls do not prove scheduling. Separate these outcomes, retain safe caseIDs, and verify no extra documents after retries/failures, including a fresh session and an independent state reconciliation.

sections.title: Delivery can repeat
sections.text:
A sender may miss the reply to an accepted request. Redelivery with the samerequestIDshould return the agreed result without another document. This differs from deduplicating similar names. Define the key’s sender/operation scope and retention policy.
Integration crosses independently failing participants. Replies can be lost after acceptance, servers can reject business rules, and schedules can repeat work. Contracts need intent identity, state, limits and unknown-outcome resolution as well as body format. Specify those cases before choosingHTTP, serialization or job APIs. A successful transport call alone cannot establish the business outcome.

Serialized input remains untrusted data. After parsing, validate schema version, required fields, types, ranges and size. Resolve external customer keys through an agreed mapping, not similar names. Never execute input or permit arbitrary addresses. A fixed local mock and synthetic payload suffice for the lab without real secrets or public external services.

sections.title: Changes have an owner
sections.text:
An extension develops a solution within defined boundaries without uncontrolled base edits. State borrowed objects and modified methods. Use an original course configuration, not a proprietary standard solution. Avoiding direct base edits does not eliminate risks to data or behavior.
Start final engineering work from an independent, bounded assignment. Define domain, model, keys, rules and observable workflows. Declare templates and own changes. Reviewers should reproduce from the package without private data. File count, code volume and attractive screens do not replace correctness, preservation and clear reasoning about accepted choices and rejected alternatives.

sections.title: Compatibility is versioned
sections.text:
Bind the extension to exact base version, compatibility mode and source hash. Changes to borrowed methods can invalidate assumptions after an upgrade. Do not claim all-future compatibility. List accepted, rejected and untested combinations; similar build numbers do not transferPASS.
Version binds source, tools, configuration format and infobase. Extensions additionally bind base configuration/dependencies. Build in fresh directories without cleaning prior work. Conflict resolution must not casually replace object identity. Preserve competing versions/requirements and prove the merged interpretation through tests. Repository operations alone are not native runtime evidence or a license to overwrite user work.

sections.title: Data can outlive code
sections.text:
Disabling an extension changes behavior and can affect access to its data. Identify extension-owned fields and records first. Never test disabling on the only work. Preserve a backup, base-only version and an independent extended copy; test reenabling too.
Cover normal behavior, failures, repeats, old-data compatibility and restore. Reproduce a transfer defect, add a discriminating test and fix a copy before rerunning baseline cases. Preserve failed history; later success never rewrites an old receipt. Distinguish untested environments, permissions and performance from proven outcomes while preserving release-gate strictness. Each conclusion binds the actual source and observed case set.

A candidate contains requirements, sourceSHA, hashes, original data, protocols and rollback. Exclude platform binaries and proprietary configurations. Defense explains contribution and evidence limits: localPASSproves neither authorship nor certification. Publication, merge and production deployment require a separate owner decision. Material readiness and official release remain distinct states even when every automated check is green.

sections.text:
A learner chooses service, warehouse, HR documents or synthetic finance. Requirements define model, operations, reports, invariants and admission. Use no real data or proprietary configurations. Study maintenance through an original training application and synthetic cases.
Start final engineering work from an independent, bounded assignment. Define domain, model, keys, rules and observable workflows. Declare templates and own changes. Reviewers should reproduce from the package without private data. File count, code volume and attractive screens do not replace correctness, preservation and clear reasoning about accepted choices and rejected alternatives.

sections.title: Present independence honestly
sections.text:
Declare templates, permitted ideas, own changes and assistance. Review ties explanation to actual code, tests and results. Local reports are editable and cannot establish authorship. NativePASSconfirms named assertions, not professional status or an official certificate.
Version binds source, tools, configuration format and infobase. Extensions additionally bind base configuration/dependencies. Build in fresh directories without cleaning prior work. Conflict resolution must not casually replace object identity. Preserve competing versions/requirements and prove the merged interpretation through tests. Repository operations alone are not native runtime evidence or a license to overwrite user work.

sections.title: A transfer defect checks understanding
sections.text:
For example, reposting doubles a total or aJOINloses a request-free customer. Reproduce, form a hypothesis and write a discriminating test first. Fix a new copy and repeat baseline cases. Transfer work must not overwrite an accepted submission or erase attempts.
Cover normal behavior, failures, repeats, old-data compatibility and restore. Reproduce a transfer defect, add a discriminating test and fix a copy before rerunning baseline cases. Preserve failed history; later success never rewrites an old receipt. Distinguish untested environments, permissions and performance from proven outcomes while preserving release-gate strictness. Each conclusion binds the actual source and observed case set.

sections.title: A defense ends with a reproducible package
sections.text:
Submit requirements, diagram, sourceSHA, dataset, positive/negative tests, performance conditions and recovery. Identify environment limits and untested areas. Pdoes not substitute forAor vice versa; a copy may share the domain model but meets independent criteria and records its own outcome.
A candidate contains requirements, sourceSHA, hashes, original data, protocols and rollback. Exclude platform binaries and proprietary configurations. Defense explains contribution and evidence limits: localPASSproves neither authorship nor certification. Publication, merge and production deployment require a separate owner decision. Material readiness and official release remain distinct states even when every automated check is green.

sections.title: First steps: platform, application and your infobase
sections.text:
First steps: platform, application and your infobase
Find or install a lawful training platform, open your own empty infobase and explain why an empty application window is the correct first result.
Be able to open a folder and a text file in Windows.
No ready-made 1C application configuration is required.

sections.title: One brand, several different things
sections.text:
“Install 1C” is an incomplete specification. The platform supplies common mechanisms: windows, infobase access, module execution and data operations. A configuration describes a domain: which customers, requests and services exist, what can be saved and how results are calculated. An infobase holds a particular application instance and its data. Several infobases can use one installed platform. A shortcut label therefore does not establish that the intended infobase is open.
In our service desk, Request as a future document type belongs to the configuration. Request REQ-001 from invented customer Alpha is data. Version 8.3.27.2214 identifies the platform. Confusing these layers can make you mistake a software update for a data transfer or submit configuration sources instead of completed work. Separate the layers before making your first change.
Think of a text editor: the installed program is not the same thing as your document. Similarly, one 1C platform installation can open several independent infobases. In this course, Training service desk is the application we build ourselves, not a third-party product to download. We begin with our own empty infobase; customers and requests appear after we define their objects.

sections.title: What an application contributes
sections.text:
The platform does not inherently know what “request closed” means. The application defines that rule. Identical words in different configurations may represent different actions. Saving generally persists an object state; posting reflects a business event according to configuration rules. Posting does not automatically mean payment or completion. A1 establishes vocabulary and a model; actual catalogs and documents are introduced in later modules.
The learning model contains three requests lasting 30, 45 and 30 minutes. Their sum is 105 minutes, but this is not yet revenue, employee workload or paid labor: we have not defined those rules. A careful user checks the meaning, unit and selection behind a metric before drawing conclusions. This habit is more useful than memorizing button positions.
A beginner has two separate questions: which application window am I using, and what has already been created in my infobase? The title and launch command answer the first. Configuration and saved data answer the second. Instructions for a different accounting or payroll application need not match an empty training infobase: commands, business rules and protected objects can differ.

sections.title: A lawful training environment
sections.text:
The main free route uses the official version for learning programming supplied by 1C. If a suitable platform is already lawfully installed, first check its version and suitability for your own training infobase. Do not copy keys, licenses or third-party configurations. The conditions of the chosen distribution apply whether you launch it from a shortcut or another tool.
The training edition is for learning and has limitations. These labs do not demonstrate a multi-user deployment, password-based access protection or real business operations. Begin with a file infobase, one session and invented records. Nexus does not redistribute the platform: obtain it from its rights holder. A professional environment is considered separately when a task actually needs one.

sections.title: Record a result that can be checked
sections.text:
Record the application name, a safe infobase alias and the full platform version separately. A configuration version does not replace a platform version. An unlabeled screenshot does not explain the operation tested. A concise protocol includes the action, expected result, observed result and limits of the conclusion.
Without an installed platform, you can study theory and classify items with the interactive diagram. This is useful preparation, but it is not 1C execution. Diagram buttons explain a model; they do not create an infobase or execute BSL. Attest a laboratory step only after observing it in the official environment.
The first observable result is deliberately concrete: your infobase appears in the startup list, Designer displays a metadata tree, and Enterprise mode opens without application sections. An empty window is normal because we have not described the application yet. Marking the lesson complete in Nexus records your self-report; it does not create a configuration or install the platform.

sections.title: Two working modes: entering data or changing the application
sections.text:
Two working modes: entering data or changing the application
Choose a mode for a task and distinguish user settings, records and configuration changes.
Your own empty training infobase from the previous lesson.
Understand the difference between platform, configuration and data.
Explain 1C:Enterprise mode and Designer.
